People management experience, including promotions, managing underperformers, hiring decisions, and compensation decisions, spanning at least one performance cycle. I enjoy training new managers, but we’re in a growth phase that requires this role to be relatively independent with hiring and performance reviews in less than a year, and I wouldn’t be able to support more first-time managers at this specific time. Two years or more of management experience are required.
Deep technical experience, not necessarily current. The successful leader needs to know how to navigate codebases, give direct and accurate feedback on code changes and PR reviews, and have demonstrated sufficient achievements as an IC managing complex logic and reusable abstractions to teach practices to others. Put another way, we value leaders who reached Staff level, worked as IC engineers developing end-to-end products for over 8 years, built libraries or frameworks from scratch, or even bounced back and forth between IC and management.
Nuanced judgment of people, situations, and business decisions. Though not always transparent from the resume, it helps if we can see that the leader has made unpopular, challenging, or unique decisions based on specific context, and didn’t just apply other people’s judgments or recipes.
Experience in an excellent (high velocity, high quality) startup environment, especially founders or Heads of Engineering. Startups at early and growth stages have different operating modes than larger companies, and managers are more shaped than other roles by their work culture. We are trying to integrate people who have lived by similar values Ashby has, and know how to promote these values in a larger business.
Managing multiple teams, projects or workstreams (nice to have). Frontline managers at Ashby lead up to 10 engineers across many teams and projects, and need to effectively delegate as well as teach project management skills instead of owning all projects themselves. Candidates with experience leading several concurrent projects with different players and business contexts will be prioritized.
